research_question: Does state-aware sequential control improve verified completion efficiency over fixed execution, fixed cascade, and simple deterministic rules after controller and switching overhead are counted?
precondition: P4 may execute only if prior experiments show material headroom for at least one adaptive decision beyond a fixed treatment.

baselines.F0_FIXED: one frozen executor/configuration until stop condition
baselines.F1_FIXED_CASCADE: frozen cheap-to-strong or equivalent deterministic escalation
baselines.F2_RULE_CONTROLLER: simple deterministic state rules frozen before execution
baselines.F3_LLM_CONTROLLER: LLM chooses only from the frozen action set using structured state
baselines.F4_LEARNED_POLICY: deferred until enough logged trajectories exist
baselines.ORACLE: retrospective policy used for headroom/regret analysis only

execution_order: P4-B LLM controller only if P4-A leaves material oracle headroom
P4-C learned policy only if logged evidence volume and residual headroom justify it
secondary_metrics: decision regret versus retrospective oracle where estimable
control_tax: All controller inference, state serialization, candidate scoring, switching, handoff, verification, and retry overhead enters total cost.
anti_bias_rules: LEARNED_POLICY is not assumed superior to deterministic rules
LLM_CONTROLLER is not assumed superior to fixed cascade
A more complex controller is prohibited unless the immediately simpler baseline leaves material measured headroom
No transcript dump is provided to the controller by default; use frozen structured state
Controller complexity may be removed even if previously implemented
holdout: Frozen unseen tasks required before mandatory adaptive controller promotion
